text.p: Italian debt markets looked pale and weak as concerns over prospects for European economic and monetary union (EMU) continued to buffet them in choppy trade.

Italy was going backwards while other European markets progressed and dealers said technically-inspired selling on the break of 130.10 support on the March future on LIFFE had added to the downward spiral.
The March future was 44 basis points lower at 129.79 with support now plotted at 129.50 and then the range bottom at 129.30. Resistance sat at 129.80 and then at the old 130.10 support point.
The November 2006 Btp was 19 basis points off at 103.77 and yielding 7.32 percent with the spread over the benchmark Bund yawning out to 182 basis points from the 170s yesterday.

Brokers noted comments from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi about unforeseeable effects if EMU were to be delayed. Prodi insisted Rome would not ask for EMU delay or easy terms to join a single currency and said the government would issue its three-year rolling plan of economic targets (DPEF) by May 15.
But brokers say concern problem continues to lie less with Italy, as such, than with Germany's will to see the EMU process through at the projected 1999 start date.

"Everyone bought the Btp because of the narrowing of the spread against Germany but if there's a delay that's no longer valid. Potentially there is more room for interest rate cuts in Italy but not with concerns over EMU delay. Nobody has really got an idea of what to do now," one broker said.
As a result some saw the Btp future sticking in a broad 129.30 to 131.20 range for now.
